Interactive Web GIS & Agricultural Analytics with the Rwapor Shiny Dashboard

Source: vignettes/shiny-dashboard.Rmd
shiny-dashboard.Rmd

Introduction

The Rwapor package includes a full-featured, reactive Shiny Web GIS dashboard designed for point-and-click satellite data retrieval, FAO-56 crop water productivity modeling, seasonal comparisons, and high-throughput farm monitoring.

1. Launching the Dashboard

Launch the dashboard directly from your R console:

library(Rwapor)

# Launch default dashboard
run_wapor()

# Or specify a custom data directory
run_wapor(data_folder = "C:/WaPOR_Projects")

The application automatically opens in your default web browser.

2. Dashboard Architecture & Modules 

┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        Rwapor Shiny Dashboard                          │
├──────────────┬──────────────┬──────────────────────────┬───────────────┤
│ 📥 Download  │ 🌾 Seasonal  │ 📊 Visualisation         │ 🛰️ Field     │
│  & Extraction│   Analysis   │  & Time Series Analysis  │   Monitoring  │
└──────────────┴──────────────┴──────────────────────────┴───────────────┘

3. Module Walkthroughs

📥 3.1 Download & Spatial Extraction Tab

  1. Project Folder: Select or browse for your project workspace. All downloaded rasters and metadata are organized hierarchically by variable and period.
  2. Interactive Area of Interest (AOI):
    • Draw on Map: Draw rectangles or arbitrary polygons directly on the Leaflet map.
    • Upload Spatial File: Ingest Shapefiles (.shp in .zip), GeoJSON, KML, GeoPackage (.gpkg), or GeoTIFF templates.
    • Smart L3 Region Auto-Detection: When Level 3 variables are selected, the app intersects your AOI geometry with all 30+ sub-national WaPOR Level 3 irrigation schemes in Africa and the Near East, filtering and auto-selecting the appropriate scheme.
  3. Variable Selection & Date Ranges:
    • Choose from 100+ WaPOR v3 and AgERA5 variables across Level 1 (~300m), Level 2 (~100m), and Level 3 (~20m).
    • Set custom start and end dates.
  4. Execution:
    • Stream raster data directly into local GeoTIFFs or extract polygon zonal time series in parallel.

🌾 3.2 Seasonal Analysis & Crop Water Productivity Hub

The Seasonal Analysis module provides a structured 4-step wizard for configuring, parameterizing, and computing agricultural water performance metrics:

  1. Step 1: Seasonal Calendar & Batch Mode:
    • Single Season vs. Batch Mode: Toggle between single-season dates or a multi-season schedule (Label, Start, End).
    • Smart Folder Detection (Detect): Auto-scans downloaded dekadal rasters in your project directory to deduce available time ranges.
    • Download Sync (Copy DL): Instantly imports the temporal periods configured in the Download tab.
    • Interactive Batch Guide ([?] Batch Guide): Built-in modal explaining batch syntax, directory layouts, and auto-linking naming conventions.
  2. Step 2: Spatial Masks & Timing:
    • Crop Masking: Support for single-crop AOIs or multi-crop categorical masks (1 = Wheat, 2 = Maize, etc.).
    • Phenological Timing (SOS/EOS): Supply pixel-wise Day of Year (DOY) planting and harvesting rasters. Cross-year seasons (EOS<SOS\text{EOS} < \text{SOS}) are automatically shifted by 365/366 days.
    • Custom Vector & CSV Generation: Collapsible panel to build all required seasonal rasters from parcel polygons (.geojson/.shp) and survey planting spreadsheets (.csv) via wapor_vector_to_season_rasters().
    • Latitude-Aware Area Weighting: Exact ellipsoidal pixel surface area weighting (cos(lat)) for distortion-free volumetric aggregations.
  3. Step 3: Crop Parameterization:
    • FAO-56 Presets: Choose from 12 pre-configured crops (Winter Wheat, Sorghum, Sugarbeet, Maize, Rice, Cotton, Potato, Soybean, Sunflower, Barley, Alfalfa, Sugarcane).
    • Multi-Crop Table Editor: Customize crop coefficients (Kc,ini,Kc,mid,Kc,endK_{c,\text{ini}}, K_{c,\text{mid}}, K_{c,\text{end}}), stage lengths, Harvest Index (HIHI), and Moisture Content (MCMC) per crop class.
  4. Step 4: Thematic Indicator Selection: Indicators are organized into four logical thematic fieldsets with quick-select controls ([Core], [All], [Clear]):
    • Evapotranspiration & Consumptive Use: Seasonal AETIAETI, Reference RETRET, Transpiration TT, and Crop Evapotranspiration (ETcET_c, including class-level rasters).
    • Agricultural Water Adequacy: Water Adequacy vs. RET (AETI/RETAETI/RET), Adequacy vs. ETc (AETI/ETcAETI/ET_c), and Relative Water Deficit (1−AETI/ETc1 - AETI/ET_c).
    • Water Accounting & Precipitation: Seasonal Precipitation (PCPPCP), Effective Precipitation (PeffP_{eff} via USDA SCS or FAO methods), and Net Irrigation Requirement (NIR=max⁡(0,ETc−Peff)NIR = \max(0, ET_c - P_{eff})).
    • Biomass Productivity & Uniformity: Seasonal NPPNPP, Crop Water Productivity (CWPCWP), Biomass Water Productivity (BWPBWP), Beneficial Transpiration Fraction (T/AETIT/AETI), and Uniformity (CVCV, Theil Disparity Index).
    • Dynamic L3 Coverage Policy: Conditionally rendered only when sub-national Level 3 datasets are selected.
  5. Execution & Export:
    • Real-time progress bar tracking multi-season execution.
    • Unified summary metrics table and one-click export of GeoTIFF rasters and CSV tables.

[!TIP] For advanced scripting and multi-crop batch workflows, see the dedicated Batch Seasonal Analysis Tutorial.

📊 3.3 Visualisation & Time Series Hub

The unified Visualisation tab combines spatial raster exploration, side-by-side comparison, and field-level time series diagnostics:

  • Single Map Visualizer: Interactive Leaflet map with real-time cursor hover values, coordinate readouts, and perceptually uniform color palettes (Viridis, Turbo, Spectral, Plasma).
  • Dual Map Split-Screen Swipe Slider: Compare two rasters side-by-side (e.g. AETIAETI vs. ETcET_c, or 2021 vs. 2022) with a draggable swipe bar to pinpoint localized water stress hotspots.
  • Zonal Time Series & Phenology: Extract and plot multi-field time series trajectories, compute running means, and decompose seasonal cycles using interactive Plotly graphics.
  • Seasonal Comparison & Anomaly Distribution: Multi-year violin and box plots comparing water productivity across cropping seasons and field parcels.

🛰️ 3.4 High-Throughput Field Monitoring (DuckDB)

  • Parcels Ingestion: Import agricultural field polygons and crop rotation records.
  • Embedded DuckDB Engine: Synchronize WaPOR satellite data with a local embedded analytical database.
  • Field Diagnostics: Run interactive SQL queries, temporal water stress anomaly checks, and border pixel filtering to ensure pure crop canopy signals.
